title: RAG Query Rewrite
content:
# RAG Query Rewrite

Query Rewrite rewrites a conversational question into a retrieval friendly query. It removes greetings, resolves pronouns with the session summary, extracts keywords, decomposes complex questions into sub queries, and labels intent such as QA, summary, comparison, or calculation. In LiveKnowledge it runs before vector search, full text search, HyDE, and graph expansion, so downstream retrieval receives cleaner search terms.

Key terms: query rewrite, sub query, intent, session summary, keywords.

title: HyDE Retrieval
content:
# HyDE Retrieval

HyDE creates a short hypothetical answer for vague or short questions. The answer is embedded and used as an additional semantic retrieval query. This helps when the original query has too few concrete terms. LiveKnowledge keeps the original query for keyword retrieval while using the HyDE vector as an auxiliary semantic signal.

Key terms: hyde, hypothetical answer, ambiguous question, embedding.

title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
content:
# Reciprocal Rank Fusion

Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines ranked lists from multiple retrievers. Each document receives a score based on 1 divided by k plus its rank. The method is robust when vector search, full text search, and graph search return different but useful candidates. LiveKnowledge applies RRF before reranking.

Key terms: rrf, reciprocal rank fusion, rank, fusion, k.

title: RAG Rerank
content:
# RAG Rerank

Rerank evaluates fused retrieval candidates and keeps the most useful evidence for the final prompt. A lightweight model scores whether a chunk can answer the user question. This reduces unrelated context and improves the evidence density of the final RAG prompt.

Key terms: rerank, relevance score, top n, evidence.

title: pgvector Indexing
content:
# pgvector Indexing

pgvector stores dense embedding vectors in PostgreSQL and supports nearest neighbor search. LiveKnowledge stores note chunks with source id, chunk index, metadata, and embedding vector. Vector search retrieves semantically similar chunks and is one branch of the hybrid retrieval pipeline.

Key terms: pgvector, embedding, cosine, hnsw, vector search.

title: PostgreSQL Full Text Search
content:
# PostgreSQL Full Text Search

PostgreSQL full text search indexes note titles and content with a tsvector column. It is useful for exact keywords, technical terms, abbreviations, and names that may not be captured reliably by embeddings. LiveKnowledge also has an ILIKE fallback for simple keyword matching.

Key terms: full text search, tsvector, keyword, ilike, postgresql.

title: Neo4j Graph Retrieval
content:
# Neo4j Graph Retrieval

Neo4j stores concepts and relations such as prerequisite, part of, related to, and contrasts with. Graph retrieval expands from extracted entities to neighboring concepts and relation paths. This helps answer questions requiring relationships across notes, cards, and concepts.

Key terms: neo4j, concept, relation, graph search, local search.

title: RAG Context Budget
content:
# RAG Context Budget

Context budget control limits the amount of retrieved material injected into the system prompt. LiveKnowledge deduplicates by source, keeps high ranking evidence first, and stops when the estimated token budget is exhausted. This reduces prompt cost and avoids burying useful evidence under redundant chunks.

Key terms: context budget, token budget, dedupe, source id, prompt.

title: Structure Aware Chunking
content:
# Structure Aware Chunking

Structure aware chunking splits Markdown by headings and plain text by paragraphs or sentence boundaries. Each chunk keeps metadata such as source id, chunk index, heading path, start index, and end index. Overlap preserves local continuity while keeping chunks small enough for embedding.

Key terms: chunking, markdown, heading path, overlap, metadata.

title: Incremental Indexing
content:
# Incremental Indexing

Incremental indexing compares normalized chunk hashes before calling the embedding provider. Unchanged chunks are skipped, changed chunks are embedded again, and deleted chunks are removed. This avoids repeated embedding calls and makes document updates faster.

Key terms: incremental indexing, content hash, chunk hash, skip embedding, upsert.

title: Batch Embedding
content:
# Batch Embedding

Batch embedding sends multiple chunk texts in one request to reduce per request overhead. LiveKnowledge groups chunks before inserting embedding records. This is especially useful when indexing many notes or long documents.

Key terms: batch embedding, batch size, api call, latency.

title: AI Provider Abstraction
content:
# AI Provider Abstraction

The AI Provider abstraction hides differences between OpenAI compatible services. It records base URL, model id, purpose, streaming support, reasoning support, vision support, context window, and embedding dimensions. User API keys are encrypted before storage.

Key terms: provider, openai, deepseek, zhipu, moonshot, qwen.

title: SSE Streaming Chat
content:
# SSE Streaming Chat

SSE streaming chat sends model output tokens to the frontend as they arrive. LiveKnowledge supports aborting generation, regenerating assistant messages, editing and resending user messages, and displaying reasoning or thinking content separately from final answer text.

Key terms: sse, streaming, abort, regenerate, thinking.

title: Persona Prompt System
content:
# Persona Prompt System

Personas define system prompt templates and teaching styles. A session can switch persona while retaining a context summary. This lets the assistant behave as a direct tutor, Socratic tutor, or scaffolded mentor while using the same knowledge base.

Key terms: persona, system prompt, teaching style, session context.

title: Cognitive Profile
content:
# Cognitive Profile

The cognitive profile summarizes learning style, attention span, preferred difficulty, domain mastery, and weak points. The chat prompt can use this summary to adjust explanation depth, pace, and review suggestions without exposing raw profile fields to the user.

Key terms: cognitive profile, learning style, attention span, mastery, weak point.

title: Knowledge Extraction Job
content:
# Knowledge Extraction Job

Knowledge extraction turns notes, conversations, or documents into summaries, flashcards, entities, and relations. Each job records input snapshot, content hash, status, current step, logs, output, and user adoption metadata. This makes AI generated knowledge auditable.

Key terms: extraction job, summary, flashcard, entity, relation, logs.

title: Flashcard Generation
content:
# Flashcard Generation

Flashcard generation creates question and answer pairs from extracted learning material. Users can preview generated cards and adopt selected results into the review system. Cards may link back to notes and concepts for traceability.

Key terms: flashcard, front, back, adopt, note.

title: SSP-MMC Half Life Review
content:
# SSP-MMC Half Life Review

The review scheduler uses a memory half life model. A card rating updates difficulty, half life, retrievability, lapse count, and next review time. Again shortens half life and increases difficulty, while Good and Easy extend the interval.

Key terms: half life, retrievability, difficulty, again, good.

title: Review Queue API
content:
# Review Queue API

The review queue selects cards whose next review time is due, orders them for practice, records each rating and response time, and updates the card state. Review logs preserve half life before and after each rating.

Key terms: review queue, next review, due card, rating, history.

title: Notes Editor
content:
# Notes Editor

The note editor supports Markdown, code blocks, tags, folders, source metadata, and version conflict handling. Notes can be indexed into embeddings and used by RAG retrieval.

Key terms: note editor, markdown, latex, autosave, version.

title: File Handler
content:
# File Handler

The file handler extracts text from uploaded documents and prepares non text attachments for chat. PDF and document text can be inserted into conversation context or sent to the extraction pipeline for note and card generation.

Key terms: pdf, docx, image, url, extract text.

title: Authentication and Session
content:
# Authentication and Session

Authentication protects user data with session based access control. Routes load the authenticated user before reading notes, messages, provider settings, cards, and profile data. This keeps the local first knowledge base separated per user.

Key terms: auth, session, cookie, user, fastify.

title: Learning Dashboard
content:
# Learning Dashboard

The learning dashboard aggregates study time, review completion, streaks, note counts, card counts, domain distribution, retention, and cognitive profile summaries. It helps users inspect the health of their learning system.

Key terms: dashboard, streak, review completion, domain mastery, statistics.

title: D3 Knowledge Graph UI
content:
# D3 Knowledge Graph UI

The graph UI uses D3 force layout to render concepts, notes, cards, and tags. Users can zoom, drag, filter by node type or domain, and inspect details before jumping back to the source note or card.

Key terms: d3, force graph, node, edge, filter.

The cognitive profile summarizes learning style, attention span, preferred difficulty, domain mastery, and weak points. The chat prompt can use this summary to adjust explanation depth, pace, and review suggestions without exposing raw profile fields to the user.

Cross reference terms: persona, system prompt; cognitive profile, learning style.

title: Persona Prompt System Related Note 2
content:
# Persona Prompt System Related Note 2

This note mentions Persona Prompt System but mainly discusses Knowledge Extraction Job.

Knowledge extraction turns notes, conversations, or documents into summaries, flashcards, entities, and relations. Each job records input snapshot, content hash, status, current step, logs, output, and user adoption metadata. This makes AI generated knowledge auditable.

Cross reference terms: persona, system prompt; extraction job, summary.

title: Persona Prompt System Related Note 3
content:
# Persona Prompt System Related Note 3

This note mentions Persona Prompt System but mainly discusses Flashcard Generation.

Flashcard generation creates question and answer pairs from extracted learning material. Users can preview generated cards and adopt selected results into the review system. Cards may link back to notes and concepts for traceability.

Cross reference terms: persona, system prompt; flashcard, front.

title: Persona Prompt System Related Note 4
content:
# Persona Prompt System Related Note 4

This note mentions Persona Prompt System but mainly discusses SSP-MMC Half Life Review.

The review scheduler uses a memory half life model. A card rating updates difficulty, half life, retrievability, lapse count, and next review time. Again shortens half life and increases difficulty, while Good and Easy extend the interval.

Cross reference terms: persona, system prompt; half life, retrievability.

title: File Handler Related Note 4
content:
# File Handler Related Note 4

This note mentions File Handler but mainly discusses RAG Query Rewrite.

Query Rewrite rewrites a conversational question into a retrieval friendly query. It removes greetings, resolves pronouns with the session summary, extracts keywords, decomposes complex questions into sub queries, and labels intent such as QA, summary, comparison, or calculation. In LiveKnowledge it runs before vector search, full text search, HyDE, and graph expansion, so downstream retrieval receives cleaner search terms.

Cross reference terms: pdf, docx; query rewrite, sub query.

title: Authentication and Session Related Note 4
content:
# Authentication and Session Related Note 4

This note mentions Authentication and Session but mainly discusses HyDE Retrieval.

HyDE creates a short hypothetical answer for vague or short questions. The answer is embedded and used as an additional semantic retrieval query. This helps when the original query has too few concrete terms. LiveKnowledge keeps the original query for keyword retrieval while using the HyDE vector as an auxiliary semantic signal.

Cross reference terms: auth, session; hyde, hypothetical answer.

title: Learning Dashboard Related Note 4
content:
# Learning Dashboard Related Note 4

This note mentions Learning Dashboard but mainly discusses Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines ranked lists from multiple retrievers. Each document receives a score based on 1 divided by k plus its rank. The method is robust when vector search, full text search, and graph search return different but useful candidates. LiveKnowledge applies RRF before reranking.

Cross reference terms: dashboard, streak; rrf, reciprocal rank fusion.

# D3 Knowledge Graph UI Related Note 4

This note mentions D3 Knowledge Graph UI but mainly discusses RAG Rerank.

Rerank evaluates fused retrieval candidates and keeps the most useful evidence for the final prompt. A lightweight model scores whether a chunk can answer the user question. This reduces unrelated context and improves the evidence density of the final RAG prompt.
